Thanks Alex 2 2for the note and the ICS. Quick heads-up: when I opened the forwarded .ics in Gmail, Google Calendar displayed the slot as Tue 24 Aug 10:00 AM PDT for me (Im in San Francisco). Thats a classic "floating time" / TZ ID strip issue when ICS files are forwarded between clients.

Two quick options that avoid the ambiguity:
1) Send the invite with an explicit timezone tag (e.g., Europe/London) or
2) Send the time in UTC in the body (e.g., Tue 24 Aug, 14:00 UTC) and Ill create the invite from our side.

Marissa, can you confirm whether we should create the invite from our calendar (so timezone info sticks) or accept Alex's ICS? Also note this week DST transitions in APAC make some of our regional teammates see different local blocks.

Saw the ICS Alex sent. Weve run into the "TZID stripped on forward" problem before: some calendar clients (esp. when an invite is forwarded as an attachment) convert the event to a floating time or anchor it to the recipients locale incorrectly. That explains why Karthik saw 10:00 AM PDT.

Given Acme spans EMEA and we have regional folks in APAC that will join, my recommendation:
- Karthik, please create the meeting on Redwood calendar and set it explicitly to Europe/London (15:00 BST). That preserves the TZID.
- In the invite description, also include the UTC time (14:00 UTC) and a note: "If your calendar shows a different local time, please confirm."

If wed rather avoid calendar friction, we can also use a short Join link (Zoom/Meet) and state the time in UTC in the body; Ill add a reminder for APAC teammates to check local conversion around DST boundaries.

Ill hold Wed 25 Aug 10:00 BST as a backup.
